bihar_raw_news.title: NTPC, EDF sign pact to develop renewable energy projects in India - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 NTPC, EDF sign pact to develop renewable energy projects in India Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service State-owned NTPC and EDF Power Solutions India have joined hands to jointly develop, own and operate pumped storage projects, hydropower projects, as well as other renewable energy (RE) projects and distribution business. This 50:50 JV shall undertake projects within India and neighbouring countries, NTPC said in a statement. The joint venture (JV) agreement was signed on September 25 in the presence of NTPC Chairman Gurdeep Singh and Bernard Fontana, Chairman and CEO of EDF SA, France. Through this strategic partnership, NTPC and EDF Power Solutions, a fully owned subsidiary of the French electricity company EDF (Électricité de France), are committed to establishing a responsible and innovative industrial company to develop, build and operate low-carbon power plants, as well as flexibility solutions and transmission assets. EDF and NTPC will leverage their respective expertise to provide tailor-made offers, drive the decarbonisation and global performance of electrical systems, aligned with India’s ambitious goals of 100 GW installed capacity of pumped storage projects by 2036. Considering their expertise and resources, both entities are poised to contribute significantly to India’s renewable energy market, driving innovation and fostering environmental stewardship. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Govt launches National Digital Tourism Stack with ONDC - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 Govt launches National Digital Tourism Stack to build digital public infrastructure for tourism Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Photo Credits: PTI The Centre on Sunday launched an initiative to build a national digital public infrastructure for tourism that will bring a wide range of travel products and services onto a shared digital ecosystem. The Ministry of Tourism has partnered with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to develop the National Digital Tourism Stack , which aims to onboard 23,000 tourism experiences and homestays and make them discoverable, trustable and bookable by the end of 2028, officials said. Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Shekhawat launched the project at Bharat Mandapam during an event marking World Tourism Day. The initiative, being developed with ONDC and supported by the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), is aimed at making India's tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy, the ministry said. The shared infrastructure will enable tourism providers to make their offerings available across participating platforms, with features including verified identities and supplier credentials, search and discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal. The programme will be implemented in phases in collaboration with the ministry, states, Union territories and the tourism industry. Tourism Secretary Bhuvnesh Kumar said artificial intelligence would form the front end of the project, with a vision of "One ticket, One pass" to bring different components of a tourist's journey together. "Currently, flights, hotels, cabs, boat rides, or even an 'aarti' at a temple, etc., need to be booked through different websites. This fragmentation makes the process a digitally painful experience for a tourist planning to visit places," Kumar said. The digital stack is intended to bring such services together through a unified digital ecosystem, he said. "The project has been approved, and we will start onboarding services. The ministry would be the catalyst and lead for this project. We will work with states and UTs to curate and validate experiences," Kumar said. A steering committee will be constituted for the initiative, Kumar said, inviting tourism stakeholders to participate. According to a flyer shared at the event, the onboarding target of 23,000 includes 14,000 tourism experiences and 9,000 homestays. Kumar said the initiative would also focus on tourism experiences that are not currently available online or have only a limited digital presence. The objective is to make travel to both major cities and smaller towns "easy, safe, and in one's preferred language", according to the project note. The digital public infrastructure is expected to help tourists discover more destinations, travel with greater confidence, book and pay conveniently and reduce paperwork. The preparation and development phase will run from October to December 2026, followed by a pilot phase from January to June 2027, during which the first batch of experiences and homestays will go live, Kumar said. The initiative will then be scaled up from July 2027 to December 2028 through a nationwide supply onboarding drive. The ministry also released the India Tourism Statistics

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor in 2025 are bold examples of India’s zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism. The Prime Minister was addressing the nation in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme on Akashvani today. He said, the surgical strikes carried out by the Indian Army on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan in 2016 demonstrated to the world a new approach to India’s counter-terrorism policy. Mr Modi said India will mark the tenth anniversary of the cross-border surgical strike tomorrow. Speaking about Census 2027, Mr Modi said the first phase of the ongoing exercise is nearing completion across all States and Union Territories. He said data from more than 32 crore families has already been recorded so far. He urged people to participate in the drive and use self-enumeration facility. Mr Modi also called for greater public participation in cleanliness drives ahead of the birth anniversary of Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi on 2nd October. He cited examples of cleanliness initiatives from across the country. Prime Minister Modi said millions of young people have pledged to stay away from drugs under the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. He called for collective efforts to build a drug-free youth, while announcing health check-ups and meditation camps as part of the 100-week campaign. Speaking about One District, One Product initiative, Prime Minister Modi said it is creating new opportunities for amla growers and entrepreneurs at Pratapgarh in Uttar Pradesh, with around 100 processing units now operational and women’s self-help groups playing an important role. He said the initiative aims to take local products to national and global markets and urged people to promote the ‘Vocal for Local’ message during the upcoming festive season.

national_raw_news.title: IAF commences operational phase of exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: IAF commences operational phase of exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर IAF commences operational phase of exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur ANI | Updated: Sep 28, 2026 03:23 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Jodhpur (Rajasthan) [India], September 28 (ANI): The Indian Air Force (IAF) on Sunday commenced the operational phase of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur following the inaugural ceremony held yesterday. Being conducted from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multilateral air exercise is themed “Power in Partnership”, underscoring the strength that comes from working together, sharing expertise, and building interoperability among partner air forces. According to the Ministry of Defence , seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) — Australia, the United States of America, the United Arab Emirates, France, Germany, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh — are participating in the exercise. The foreign aircraft taking part include the F-35 Lightning II, Rafale, F-16, A400M, MRTT, C-130, C-130J and KC-30A, bringing together a diverse mix of combat, airlift and air-to-air refuelling capabilities. Building on the successful inaugural edition in 2024, Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides participating air forces an opportunity for advanced joint training, exchange of operational expertise and consolidation of professional experience. The participating contingents will operate alongside the IAF, employing frontline combat platforms and support elements across a range of missions. Several other FFCs will also participate as observers. The ministry said that the exercise will facilitate professional interaction among aircrew, mission planners and operational support personnel, with emphasis on interoperability, mutual learning, aerospace safety and enhanced understanding of operational procedures. The interaction will provide participating forces an opportunity to operate together, share experiences and gain a better understanding of each other's capabilities and operating philosophies. This edition of Tarang Shakti has a wider canvas beyond flying operations, with a range of professional, cultural and outreach activities planned during the exercise. These include a dedicated seminar, an industrial tour for the participating foreign contingents, the Sekhon Marathon, heritage tours, and yoga sessions. These engagements will provide opportunities for professional exchange, exposure to India's aerospace and industrial ecosystem, and greater interaction and camaraderie among the participating contingents. Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides the IAF an opportunity to demonstrate its operational capabilities, professional standards and institutional ethos, while highlighting India's growing indigenous aerospace and defence capabilities. The exercise, under the theme “Power in Partnership”, reinforces the importance of cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust in building enduring partnerships among participating air forces. The exercise reaffirms India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and enhanced military cooperation in support of regional peace, security and stability, while strengthening partnerships and fostering greater strategic cooperation through shared operational experience.
